title: fix(driver-turso): converge remote date/json cells the pre-fix batch door stored unconverted
body:
Fixes #19868

Clause-②: no

## What this changes

Every remote Turso schema door ends in `completeRemoteSchemaSync`. It now runs a second backfill after the canonical temporal one. The new pass converges the `date` and `json` cells that the pre-#19844 `syncSchemasBatch` door stored without `formatInput`. It rewrites only the cells whose stored text already determines their value.

**Disposition of the residue the card's title names (seat decision, after the dev's report):** a stored `true` reading back as `1`, a string `'42'` reading back as `42`, and a string `'true'` reading back as `true` have bytes identical to another writer's. That is the class the maintainer's ruling of 2026-08-26 on #12380 already settled for the local face (`packages/drivers/driver-sql/CHANGELOG.md`: "The class stops growing; it is not retroactively repaired.", "with that cost accepted explicitly"), for the same reason ("No migration can know which was written"). A new branch of a ruled class reuses that ruling with its reason, so it is the answer on the remote face too: this PR converges every exactly recoverable class, discloses the rest in its changeset, and closes the card. The first line was changed from `Refs` to `Fixes` by the seat accordingly.

## Recoverability, measured (A1/A2)

The pre-fix arm was run on the `libsql` SQLite double: `RemoteTransport.syncSchemasBatch` alone, then `create` with no registration. The fixed driver then booted over the same database through `syncSchemasBatch`. The json column is TEXT affinity, so every scalar lands as TEXT and `typeof` separates nothing. The Turso-wire column comes from `@libsql/client`'s hrana encoder, read in `node_modules`: a JS number is sent as `float`, and a boolean as `integer` `1n`/`0n`. The double's better-sqlite3 binds a JS number (and the stub's `true` → `1`) as REAL. Both shapes were measured into a TEXT column.

| written (pre-fix) | cell on the double | cell on the Turso wire | fixed read | fixed door stores | rewritten? |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| json `'hello'` | TEXT `hello` (`json_valid` 0) | same | `'hello'` | `"hello"` | **yes**, read unchanged |
| json `''` | TEXT empty (`json_valid` 0) | same | `''` | `""` | **yes**, read unchanged |
| json `true` / `false` | TEXT `1.0` / `0.0` | TEXT `1` / `0` | `1` / `0` | `true` / `false` | no. `1.0` is also a pre-fix number `1`. `1` is also a pre-fix string `'1'` and the fixed door's number `1` |
| json `0` / `1` / `42` | TEXT `0.0` / `1.0` / `42.0` | same | `0` / `1` / `42` (correct) | `0` / `1` / `42` | no (a pre-fix string `'42.0'` leaves the same bytes) |
| json `'42'` | TEXT `42` | same | `42` | `"42"` | no. `42` is what the fixed door stores for the number `42` |
| json `'true'` | TEXT `true` | same | `true` | `"true"` | no. `true` is what the fixed door stores for the boolean `true` |
| json `null` | NULL | same | `null` | NULL | already canonical |
| date `Date` (UTC midnight) | `2025-07-28T00:00:00.000Z` | same | `2025-07-28` | `2025-07-28` | **yes** |
| date `Date` = UTC+8 local midnight of 07-28 | `2025-07-27T16:00:00.000Z` | same | `2025-07-27` | `2025-07-27` | **yes**, to `2025-07-27` (see below) |
| date `…Z` / `+08:00` / `-05:00` / zone-naive (space or `T`) / leading or trailing space | the text as sent | same | its leading `YYYY-MM-DD` | its leading `YYYY-MM-DD` | **yes** |
| date epoch number / non-date text / bare day | same bytes from both doors | same | as stored | as stored | not residue |

On the `date` question in A2: a full timestamp maps to exactly one day under the codec. `SqlDriver.toDateOnly` takes the LEADING day of a string (so `2025-07-28T23:30:00-05:00` is `2025-07-28`, not the UTC `07-29`) and the UTC day of a `Date`. A `Date` built at local midnight east of UTC therefore already reads, and is already written by the fixed door, as the previous day. Measured with `new Date(2025, 6, 28)` under `TZ=Asia/Shanghai`: stored `2025-07-27T16:00:00.000Z`, read `2025-07-27`, and the fixed door stores `2025-07-27`. The writer's zone is not in the cell, so the day the caller meant is not recoverable by any door. This PR writes the day the codec already answers and does not try to recover the caller's.

The invariant the change keeps: **it rewrites a cell only when the fixed READ already answers a determined value, and it writes the fixed WRITE door's form of that value.** No converted cell reads differently afterwards; that is pinned. What changes is what a filter compares. Before the boot, `{ d: '2025-07-28' }` matched only the bare-day row. After it, the filter also matches all 8 full-timestamp rows whose day is 07-28, and `{ d: '2025-07-27' }` matches the UTC+8 row, which it missed before.

## Landing site and design

- `packages/drivers/driver-turso/src/remote-codec-residue-backfill.ts` (new): the pass.
  - **SQL only pre-filters**, cheaply enough for every boot. For json, a candidate is TEXT with `json_valid() = 0`. For date, it is TEXT longer than 10 characters whose left-trimmed first 10 characters glob as `YYYY-MM-DD`; the trim uses the exact `String.prototype.trim` set, bound as an argument.
  - **The driver's own codec decides and computes the new value**, handed over and not copied. For json that is `JSON.parse` / `JSON.stringify`, the `formatOutput` / `formatInput` json arms. For date it is `SqlDriver.toDateOnly`.
  - **Each write is compare-and-set** on the text it was computed from.
  - The pass is batched by a `rowid` cursor and reuses the temporal backfill's `batchSize` and `maxBatches` defaults, 500 × 20. It is resumable: a budget-stopped column is unmarked and resumes at the next sync. A second boot writes nothing.
  - It is quiet: nothing throws out of it, and failures are logged at `warn`.
  - The probe is one `SELECT` per table, and all tables go out in one round-trip.
- `turso-driver.ts`: `completeRemoteSchemaSync` calls `backfillRemoteCodecResidueQuietly()` after the temporal backfill, which calls the private `backfillRemoteCodecResidue()`. Per-process marks live in `remoteCodecResidueConverged`. No public surface was added: the module is not exported from `index.ts`, and the method is private.
- Deliberately excluded:
  - **Single-value media columns.** Their quoted-or-bare id form is an ADR-0104 deployment fact the remote doors never ask about, and both forms read the same.
  - **JSON nested past SQLite's JSON depth limit.** Measured on SQLite 3.53.4, `json_valid()` answers 0 at 1001 levels and `JSON.parse` reads it. It is withheld, because re-quoting it would turn an array into a string. The codec, not SQLite, decides.
- `packages/drivers/driver-sql` is **not** touched. No helper was shared: the local face's `backfillCanonicalJsonEncoding` is a Knex `UPDATE`, and this pass needs a rowid walk plus a JS codec.

## A4: the local face

Measured through `TursoDriver` local (`:memory:`) `syncSchemasBatch` and `create` with the same inputs. Every `date` lands as the 10-character day and every json scalar as its JSON encoding. The local door registers field types before any write, so it has **no** residue from this door, and nothing here runs locally. Full-timestamp `date` rows written before `formatInput` gained its `date` arm would be a different producer. They were not measured here (shallow history), and they are not fixed here.

## Tests

`packages/drivers/driver-turso/src/turso-remote-codec-residue-backfill.test.ts`, 14 cases, over real SQLite cells:
- the before-state, including the card's filter miss on the fixed read path;
- every recoverable class, with its cell before, its cell after, and its read-back, plus the day filter and a `$lte` bare-day bound;
- no read changes, across every row;
- the ambiguous classes (both the double and the wire shapes), the canonical dates, `null`, a media column and deep JSON, all left byte-for-byte;
- idempotence: a second boot issues no `UPDATE` and one probe statement, and a second sync in-process issues no probe;
- a failing probe leaves the boot up and the columns unmarked;
- paging, budget and resume; compare-and-set;
- the date pre-filter equals `toDateOnly` over a corpus that includes every trim character, and `JS_TRIM_CHARS` equals the engine's own `trim` over the BMP;
- the json pre-filter is a superset whose only extra is deep JSON.

Package runs on `257ac60607` (patch round 1; round 1 on `4afdb8c170` read the same counts):
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/driver-turso test`: `Test Files 59 passed (59)` · `Tests 1331 passed (1331)`.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/driver-turso typecheck`: `tsc --noEmit`, exit 0. The package tsconfig includes `src/**/*`, so the new test file is compiled.

**Ablation** (on `4afdb8c170`; patch round 1 changed spelling and prose only, and the runtime `JS_TRIM_CHARS` string is byte-identical), run once through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`, which deleted only the wiring line `await this.backfillRemoteCodecResidueQuietly();`. The anchor went 1 → 0, and the blob went `a686f4985bc4` → `ae43cfb30ecb`. Four pins went red: the date rewrite and filter, the json re-encode, no-read-change (whose non-vacuity leg fails), and idempotence (the probe count). `Tests 4 failed | 10 passed (14)`. The restore was proven: blob `a686f4985bc4` equals HEAD, `git diff HEAD` is empty, and `git status` is clean. The source resolves through a relative import, so no `dist/` is involved.

## Gates

On `257ac60607` (patch round 1): `--commands` derived the same 61 commands (diff empty), and after a cached whole-package build all 61 exited 0 on the first pass; `--ran`: `61 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED`. `pnpm check:nul-bytes`, `node scripts/check-issue-citations.mjs` and `node scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs --base origin/main`: exit 0.

Round 1: `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands` on `4afdb8c170` derived 61 commands, each run with its exit captured before any pipe. Three first exited 3 (PREREQUISITE NOT MET: `dual-build-cjs-loads`, `lean-entry-closure`, `type-check-debt`). After building the objectql closure and all packages (`turbo run build --filter='./packages/*' --filter='./packages/*/*'`), all three exited 0. `--ran`: `61 derived famil(ies) accounted for — 61 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED`. Also by hand:
- `node scripts/check-issue-citations.mjs` (the live verdict): exit 0.
- `pnpm check:driver-conformance`: exit 0.
- `pnpm check:nul-bytes`: exit 0.
- The control-byte self-scan over the four files: no match.

## Acceptance notes

- **Out of scope, class (a), for the seat to file.** The LOCAL #12380 json backfill has the same depth hole this PR avoids. `SqlDriver.backfillCanonicalJsonEncoding` selects `json_valid(??) = 0`, so a json value nested past 1000 levels is `json_quote`d into a string on the next `syncSchema`. Reproduced on `TursoDriver` local `:memory:`: before the re-sync, `Array.isArray(row.j)` is `true`; after it, `false` (`typeof` `string`), and the cell starts with a quote character.
- Steady-state cost: remote boots now pay one more read round-trip. That is a probe scanning each managed table that has `date` or json columns, once per process. Turso bills rows read.
- The `libsql` double does not bind like the Turso wire: better-sqlite3 binds every JS number, and the stub's `true` → `1`, as REAL, while hrana sends a boolean as INTEGER. The tests pin both shapes.
- The remote schema doors never call `resolveFileColumnsMoved`, so an engine-supplied ADR-0104 resolver is never asked in remote mode. Whether a remote deployment can reach the moved state was not measured.
